sol-review.note: GPT fallback for independent review; must differ from every author and repair model.

bounded-build.description: One new feature slice, endpoint or script from a clear brief, in one or two files. Domain kinds (iOS, UI, 3D, data contract, user-facing copy) win.

quick-edit.description: Renames, small scoped refactors, lint and type fixes. No new behavior. Domain kinds (iOS, UI, 3D, data contract, user-facing copy) win.

write-tests.description: Adding or changing tests only, in any codebase, including iOS. No product code changes. A task that also fixes product code is a bug fix or multi-step coding.

docs.description: Docs for developers: READMEs, AGENTS.md, code comments and changelogs. Not copy that product users read.

scouting.description: Read-only investigation: explain code, locate files, map a repo or summarize a PR. No changes.

first-pass-review.description: A first look at Muse or tier-1 output, never the merge gate. A higher-risk review kind wins.

simple-bug-fix.description: Fix a bug whose cause is known, or obvious from the repro, with a clear and bounded fix. A stack trace or repro that points to the failing code counts as an obvious cause. Includes adding a test for it. If the cause must be found, it is hard-bug-fix.

multi-step-coding.description: A larger change across several files or long-running coding work. Includes adding tests and fixing the code they expose across several modules. Migration and the domain kinds win.

migration.description: Moving code to a new API, framework, version or structure, and large refactors. A database schema migration for one table is data-contract. Wins over multi-step-coding when the move is the main goal.

hard-bug-fix.description: Fix a bug whose cause is unknown and must be investigated, even if the symptom reproduces. If the brief says to find the cause, it is this kind. Use this when the repro or trace does not point to the cause. Includes writing tests to find unknown bugs and fixing what they expose.

ci-terminal.description: Failing pipelines, build scripts and environment fixes. Not bugs in product code.

routine-review.description: Review of tier-2 work. high-risk-review wins when the risk is higher.

skill-workflow.description: Work requiring skills such as SLOPE, ship gates, sim-lab or kit-curator; Muse follows skills poorly.

3d-work.description: 3D modeling, geometry, materials, shaders and spatial work. Wins over quick-edit, bounded-build and multi-step-coding; tests-only work is write-tests.

ui-visual.description: UI and visual design or build where the design is not settled: new screens, layout, look and feel. Wins over quick-edit, bounded-build and multi-step-coding; tests-only work is write-tests.

ios.description: Work inside an iOS app: Swift, Xcode, simulator, device and App Store problems. Wins over quick-edit, bounded-build and multi-step-coding; tests-only work is write-tests.

architecture.description: Deciding how systems or components fit together, who owns what, and how they evolve. Includes decision records about integration, versioning and compatibility between components, even when a data format is part of the decision. A decision record about how systems or components fit together is architecture even with no code. Wins over quick-edit, bounded-build and multi-step-coding; tests-only work is write-tests.

high-risk-review.description: Review of security, data contracts or UI, and anything about to merge to a deploy branch. Wins over the other review kinds.

data-contract.description: Designing or changing one specific schema, API shape or database contract, usually with code. Includes adding or changing database columns and writing their schema migrations. If the main output is a decision about structure across systems, it is architecture. Wins over quick-edit, bounded-build and multi-step-coding; tests-only work is write-tests.

bulk-text.description: Bulk, private or low-stakes text work.
bulk-text.crossTierReason: Local work falls back to tier 1 when Pi is unavailable.

image-generation.description: Image generation through Codex image tooling; pi-imagen is an alternative tool, not a route.
image-generation.crossTierReason: Image tooling uses Astra outside the paid tier choices.

user-facing-copy.description: Writing or rewriting copy a product's users read: onboarding text, chat copy, error messages and marketing. Not button labels, field names or menu items. Wins over docs, quick-edit, bounded-build and multi-step-coding; tests-only work is write-tests.

visual-implementation.description: A narrowly scoped visual or styling task with a settled design.

mac-studio.description: Mac Studio; supports Muse and the optional local server.

pc.description: PC; no Muse or pi-local route.
